chapter: Decca records, the Savoy and Moe Gale
title: The failed southern tour
summary: On a southern tour booked by Gale there was no advertising at the venues, they ran short of money and had to ask New York for more.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Had you done that before as big band.

As a southern tour, well, not on this particular part of the country, we hadn't been. We had been down to Texas and down that way, and like to take it down through Florida and all down through that southeastern and all that stuff through there.

This wasn't successful at all because everywhere we were supposed to play the guys didn't get any advertisement. They says, well, man, we got five $200 advance, said we didn't receive no placards, we didn't receive no nothing, we didn't receive nothing. So says, well, what's wrong. So then the guys would have to try to get around and do the best that they could. They said, well, bring the band up here tonight and we'll see if we can get a crowd. We'll get a truck or car or something and put the sign and ride all over town. So that's what we had to go through for about two weeks. He didn't send no nothing, so we get back to New York, well, quite naturally we had to send back to them

for money and they had this bus that we had from Jersey, whatever it was that we had carrying the whole group, so when they called me down there, Gail told me, look, now, Jay, we're going to have to run into the loan company here, we are trying to run a business here, but I said look you all goofed us up, we just got completely goofed. You have nothing -- well, whoever was supposed to have sent that out, we didn't have anything to do with that, and that we feel that's not our fault.
